plan.melodySummary: The melody travels from Flute (bright opening) to Trumpet (bold statement), then to Alto Sax and Bassoon for the flowing eighth-note passages, before returning to Flute and Trumpet for the climactic close. The dynamic arc uses terraced Baroque contrasts: !f! opening, !p! echo phrase, building to !f! at the eighth-note climax, then a stately !f! cadence.

sections.label: Phrase A
sections.notes: Play the sustained melody at a firm !f! with a light cadential trill on the final beat of m.4; keep clean Baroque articulation.

sections.label: Phrase A' (echo)
sections.notes: Restate as a terraced-dynamic echo at !p!; imitative Flute answers one bar later, also at !p!, over a quieter walking Bassoon.

sections.label: Phrase B (running eighths)
sections.notes: Drive the continuous eighth-note sequences at !f! with even, detached Baroque phrasing; lean into each step of the melodic sequence.

sections.label: Phrase C (climax & cadence)
sections.notes: Peak of the arrangement at full !f!; sustain the descending eighth-note run brilliantly and place a strong trill on m.15 before the broad final D in m.16.

Flute.instruction: Bright, agile top voice: carry the melody at !f! in mm.1-4 and mm.13-16; drop to a soft imitative countermelody at !p! entering one bar late in mm.5-8; add cadential trills.

Trumpet.instruction: State the echoed theme at !p! in mm.5-8, then serve as bold countermelody at !f! in mm.1-4 and mm.13-16; sustained inner harmony at !f! during mm.9-12.

Alto Sax.instruction: Provide functional inner harmony in mm.1-8 (matching each section's dynamic) then take the running eighth-note melody at !f! in mm.9-12 with even, detached articulation; return to harmony at !f! in mm.13-16.

Bassoon.instruction: Anchor the piece with a steady walking bass in quarters/eighths outlining the functional harmony; play !f! in mm.1-4 and mm.9-16, drop to !p! in mm.5-8, and add a short imitative countermelody figure in mm.9-12.
